whyChoose.title: What Ceres Families Should Know About California Wrongful Death Law

items.title: Only Certain Family Members Can File
items.desc: California limits who has standing to bring a wrongful death claim, prioritizing a spouse, domestic partner, and children, with other dependents or heirs eligible in some cases. An attorney can help clarify where your family fits.

items.title: A Strict Two-Year Deadline Applies
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims in California must be filed within two years of the date of death, though claims against a government entity carry a much shorter window. Missing these deadlines can permanently bar recovery.

items.title: Recoverable Losses Go Beyond Funeral Costs
items.desc: California law allows families to seek compensation for funeral and burial expenses, lost financial support, and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance. These losses are separate from any criminal case that may also result from the same incident.

items.question: How long do we have to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, California gives families two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death lawsuit. If a government entity, like a city road agency, may be involved, the deadline is much shorter and requires an early formal claim. An attorney can confirm the timeline that applies to your situation.

items.question: Who in our family is allowed to bring the claim?
items.answer: California law generally gives priority to a surviving spouse, domestic partner, and children. If none exist, other dependents or heirs may have standing depending on the circumstances. An independent attorney can review your family situation and explain who may bring the claim.

items.question: Does a wrongful death crash on a road like Mitchell Road or Whitmore Avenue affect our case differently?
items.answer: Every case depends on the specific facts, including how and where the crash occurred, not just the road name. Public crash-count data for corridors in Ceres, such as Mitchell Road and Whitmore Avenue, can sometimes be relevant background information. An attorney can review the police report and any available records to understand what happened.

items.question: Is this a law firm, and what does it cost to talk to someone?
items.answer: LawProactive is not a law firm — we're a free service that connects you with an independent personal injury attorney in the network. There's no cost to speak with an attorney, and if they take your case, it's typically handled on contingency, meaning no fee unless there's a recovery.
